gives.name: w
gives.what: minimum size of a fillet weld, as its leg dimension

takes.name: t
takes.what: material thickness of the thinner part joined

gives.name: Fn
gives.what: nominal stress of a fastener: the tensile stress Fnt, or the shear stress Fnv in a bearing-type connection

takes.name: fastener
takes.what: description of the fastener: A307 bolts, then the bolt strength groups

takes.name: stress
takes.what: which stress: tensile, shear with threads not excluded from the shear planes (N), shear with threads excluded (X)

gives.name: dh
gives.what: nominal diameter of a standard or an oversize hole

gives.name: e
gives.what: minimum edge distance from the centre of a standard hole to the edge of the connected part

not_written.what: the SI value printed in parentheses beside every US customary value: thickness limits (6), (13), (19) mm and weld sizes (3), (5), (6), (8) mm
not_written.why: two numbers in one cell. The SI numbers are rounded sizes, not conversions of the fractions, so the row holds the US customary values alone.

not_written.what: footnote [a] on the size column: the size is the leg dimension, and a weld made with electrodes that are not low-hydrogen has to be a single-pass weld
not_written.why: a requirement on how the weld is made. It is not a value and not a comparison of quantities, so a row has no place for it.
two numbers in one cell. The row holds the ksi values.

not_written.what: the sixth and last line, threaded parts meeting Section A3.4: 0.75Fu for Fnt, 0.450Fu for Fnv (N), 0.563Fu for Fnv (X)
not_written.why: a formula in Fu in place of a number. The line is left out, so the fastener key has five names, not six.

not_written.what: footnote [b] on the Fnt column: for tensile strength the tensile stress area times the specified minimum tensile stress of the material may be used in place of the tabulated value, which rests on a stress area of 0.75 times the gross area
not_written.why: a permitted alternative to every Fnt cell, taken by a choice the row cannot read. The plain values are transcribed.

not_written.what: footnote [c] on both Fnv columns: Fnv is reduced to 83.3% of the tabulated value in an end-loaded connection whose fastener pattern is longer than 38 in. (950 mm)
not_written.why: a footnote that changes the value under a condition on a length the row does not take. The plain values are transcribed.

not_written.what: footnote [d] on both shear cells of the A307 line: the value is reduced by 1% for each 1/16 in. (2 mm) of grip length over five diameters
not_written.why: a footnote that changes the value by a formula in the grip length and the diameter. The plain value 27 is transcribed.

not_written.what: footnotes [a], [e] and [f]: [a] on the Fnt column sends high-strength bolts under tensile fatigue loading to Appendix 3; [e] on the (N) column says threads are assumed and permitted in the shear planes in all cases; [f] on both shear cells of the Group 200 line says the transition area of those bolts counts as threaded
not_written.why: conditions of use, not values. None is a comparison of quantities.

not_written.what: the sixth and last line, bolt diameter 1 1/8 and larger: d + 1/8 for a standard hole, d + 5/16 for an oversize hole
not_written.why: a formula in d in place of a number, and a line that is a range of d where the others are listed sizes. The line is left out.

not_written.what: the short-slot and long-slot columns of every line
not_written.why: two numbers in one cell, a width and a length, and in the last line two formulas. Left out as tables.tsv says.

not_written.what: the eighth and last line, bolt diameter over 1 1/4: 1 1/4 times d
not_written.why: a formula in d in place of a number. The line is left out.

not_written.what: footnote [a] on the title: a lesser edge distance is permitted where Sections J3.11 and J4 are satisfied, but one under one bolt diameter needs the approval of the engineer of record
not_written.why: a footnote that changes the minimum under a condition that is not a comparison of the row's quantities. The plain values are transcribed.

not_written.what: footnote [b] on the title: oversized and slotted holes are sent to Table J3.5
not_written.why: a pointer. The row holds standard holes only and cannot state that as a condition.
